title: Teaching points apart from quiz points
statement: Where a course pays points both for teaching steps and for graded questions, keep the two apart, so a poor quiz never cancels what was earned while learning.
example: A child who works through all 18 sample lessons keeps the teaching part's 252 points however the graded questions go.
detail: A Grade 3 reading sample's points rubric, whose rules are copied from the live course's rubric, splits each lesson into a teaching part, which pays a small fixed amount for each teaching step the child finishes, and a graded part, which pays for focused minutes only if enough of the reading questions are right. The two pay separately and never mix, so a child who works hard through the teaching and then does poorly on the questions keeps everything earned while learning. A step pays only once every part asking for an answer is answered, and reading, watching a model and reflecting pay nothing, since points are for work the child produced that can be checked.
against: A Grade 5 release contract pays no points per answer and counts them once, at a successful finish that meets a 90 percent checkpoint, from whole focused minutes: "A correct response records immediate progress and feedback; it does not award per-answer XP." (grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/docs/G5_STUDENT_EXPERIENCE_RELEASE_GATE.qmd, line 37). The records points-for-focused-time-not-answers and mastery-only-for-verified-learning hold that points come once at the finish and that low-accuracy work earns nothing, which a teaching stream paid however the quiz goes does not meet.

evidence.quote: A lesson has a teaching part and a graded part. They pay separately and never mix.
